items.title: 68356_Howard R. Scott oral history interview
items.q: This fellow was named Honey Potter of Freeport, Long Island. If Honey Potter had been a businessman and had a good education, he could have made a million dollars. He had most of the work out there in Long Island.

ctx.x: Well, it so happened that in playing around, I met one of the fellows that was in the band, by the name of Cecil Smith. He was a saxophone player. He became interested in me, I don't know why. He just liked me, that's all. And talking with fellows I'd met, musicians. And he asked me, hey, Scotty, what you doing? You working? I said, no. He says, do you belong (unintelligible)? I said, no. He said, well, that's right, you're too young.

I was still in high school. He said, can you work weekends? I said, oh, yes, sure, sure, sure. He said, well, I'll tell you, you have to come a long way, down on Long Island. He says, but I'll take you out there. He had heard me play, and he said, I could do all right. This fellow was named Honey Potter of Freeport, Long Island. If Honey Potter had been a businessman and had a good education, he could have made a million dollars. He had most of the work out there in Long Island.
See, everything was live music then. There was no radio, and no -- of course, no television. Well, we used to go from Harlem and drive out to Long Island. Honey's wife --
